posts.title: Call for Speakers: Your idea belongs at the Sarasota Tech Summit
posts.summary: Share your domain expertise, discuss a hard-won lesson, lead a hands-on session, or show what you are building. Submit your idea for the February 18, 2027 Summit at Mote SEA.
posts.body:
You know something this community could use!

A technology you understand. A problem you solved. A product you built. A lesson that would have saved you six months. Bring it to the Sarasota Tech Summit on February 18, 2027 at Mote SEA.

We are inviting people from our community to share what they know, show what they are building, and lead conversations that help others move forward. First-time presenters are welcome.

→ Submit your presentation idea

What could you help someone do better?

We want practical content attendees can put to work. That could mean:

  • Build with technology: AI, cybersecurity, robotics, manufacturing, materials science, healthcare, oceanography, and other fields where new ideas are becoming real.

  • Start or grow a business: finding customers, hiring, product design, going to market, and lessons from scaling a company.

  • Try something firsthand: a working demo, hands-on training, or a discussion that helps people tackle a shared challenge.

Choose the format that fits your idea

Give a focused talk, go deeper with a full presentation, bring different perspectives together on a panel, teach a workshop, guide a roundtable, or host a demo station. The expanded space at Mote SEA gives us more ways to learn from one another. Our January event attracted over 500 people - we expect even more in 2027.

Start with the idea

Give it a working title, choose your format, and tell us what attendees will learn, experience, or take away. Complete the questions that apply to your session. You can refine the title later.

We will review proposals for relevance, practical value, and fit with the overall program. Submitting does not guarantee selection. Selected presenters need to attend in person.

→ Submit your presentation idea

The next useful connection in Sarasota could start with something you share.

P.S. Know someone whose work deserves a room? Please share this invitation.

posts.title: Your Private Invite to build the 2027 Sarasota Tech Summit
posts.summary: The Sarasota Tech Summit returns Thursday, February 18th, 2027 - and before we book a single speaker or schedule a session, you can tell us what you want in the room.
posts.body:
The 2027 Summit agenda starts with you.

The Sarasota Tech Summit returns Thursday, February 18th, 2027 - and before we book a single speaker or schedule a session, you can tell us what you want in the room.

→ Take the 2-minute survey

Here's why your input carries more weight this year:

The last Summit sold out at 500+ tickets. For 2027, we're back at Mote SEA with a much bigger footprint - the main conference space plus multiple classrooms and a large meeting room. That unlocks parallel tracks, hands-on workshops, roundtables, live demos, and a higher ticket cap.

More space means more decisions: Which topics get a track? Talks or workshops? Who should be up front? Your answers decide.

The survey takes about 3 minutes mostly multiple choice. It closes September 15th - after that, the planning team incorporates your feedback into the agenda.

→ Tell us what you want

Everyone who completes the survey gets first access to early-bird incentives before they open to the public.

Over the coming weeks we'll send out a call for speakers and instructors, sponsorship info, volunteer sign-ups, and ticket sales. But the survey comes first - everything else gets built on what you tell us.

Thanks for making the last Summit what it was. With your input, we're making Sarasota the best place to live, work, and be tech.

P.S. 2 minutes now = a February 18th Summit built around what you actually want. Survey link - closes September 15th.

posts.title: August Community Updates
posts.summary: As the summer wraps up, we have a few exciting events to highlight over the next month!
posts.body:
Hello Sarasota community! We hope you are having a wonderful summer. At Sarasota Tech, we put together the best opportunities for our community to meet, learn and collaborate. Check out these upcoming events in August and September.

Special Interest Group - Making the Most of Tech Transfer
Thursday, August 13th

Have you ever wondered how novel scientific discoveries get commercialized by the private sector? This Special Interest Group will dive into the ins and outs of tech transfer. We have assembled an expert panel representing all parties in a typical licensing transaction - the IP providers, the commercial operators and the lawyers. The University of Florida is one of the most active tech licensing programs in the country. Mote Marine Laboratory has over 45 PHD-level scientists performing unique research in ocean technologies and sea-derived products. Leaders from both of these institutions will be on our panel to dive into what tech is available and how licensing typically works.

Come learn how ground-breaking research is commercialized into new business ventures. The event will have limited capacity, so be sure to register soon.

The Shipyard Weekend Hackathon
Friday, September 4th - Sunday, September 6th

We know that Sarasota has talent. We want to get it out and build! This weekend hackathon is targeted at our younger population (ages 16 to 25). Participants will spend the Labor Day weekend collaborating on teams to create working software. We will inspire the teams with project ideas from local non-profits. After everything is built, the teams will present their work to a live audience and a panel of judges. Of course there will be prizes, but more importantly, we will showcase what the Sarasota community can produce!

Check out The Shipyard website for more program information. The event will kick off the evening of Friday, September 4th and end on Sunday afternoon, September 6th. All activities will be hosted at Ringling College.

There are multiple ways to participate:

  • Contestant. Open to young people ages 16-25 who want to spend the weekend hacking out software.

  • Mentor. We will pair each team with an experienced mentor, who will help guide the process.

  • Non-profit Idea. To keep the community focus, we will seed the project ideas with input from local organizations. Non-profits can submit ideas for software that will supercharge their mission!

  • Public Viewing. The Friday evening kick-off and Sunday afternoon demos will be open to the public. Business leaders, investors, hiring managers, community supporters and Sarasota lovers are all welcome to attend. Who knows? You might find your next team member or start-up founder amongst the contestants.

Registration forms for the various roles are available on the event program page. There are also sponsorship opportunities for organizations that want to get more involved and show their support.

September Tech JAM - The Rosemary
Thursday, September 17th

After a summer break, our next Tech JAM will be in the Rosemary district. The event is open for registration now. Exact location and format will be announced as the date approaches. Join the area's best networking event for tech professionals!

Summit 2027 - Coming Soon!

Sarasota Tech will be back at Mote SEA in February 2027 for an even bigger and better Summit conference! Look for upcoming announcements with event information. Similar to our prior conference in January, we want to showcase the best of the Sarasota community. There will be many opportunities to get involved, as speakers, instructors, volunteers and sponsors. We will be sending out more information and calls to action soon.

posts.title: Attend Goalmaxxing with AI and Special Interest Groups (SIGs)
posts.summary: Our next Special Interest Group lands Wednesday, July 15: learn to direct AI agents to do real work. Included with premium membership, along with every SIG and the annual Summit.
posts.body:
The biggest productivity gain in tech right now comes from a new skill: directing AI agents to do work you used to grind through yourself.

That skill is the focus of our next Special Interest Group, Goalmaxxing with AI, on Wednesday, July 15. In one session you'll learn how to hand an agent the coding or research you'd normally do alone, structure its output as clear goals, and keep it producing at full capacity. That last part is the craft we call Goalmaxxing. You'll walk out with an approach you can apply to your own work the next morning.

Sarasota Tech Premium members can register now.

If you've been to a Tech JAM, you know we can fill a room. Several hundred of you show up on the third Thursday of every month to meet, trade ideas, and find collaborators. The JAMs aren't going anywhere. But many of you asked for a second track: fewer name tags, more depth, and a skill you can use on Monday. So we created Special Interest Groups.

The first two proved the format. Vibe Coding and Agentic AI earned some of the strongest feedback we've collected for any event, and attendees are already applying what they learned in their day jobs. Goalmaxxing is the third, and it goes straight at the question we hear most: how do I actually get an agent to do useful work for me?

One membership, every SIG, plus the Summit

Premium membership is what keeps all of this running. For $250 a year (renews annually), you get:

  • A seat at every Special Interest Group we run, starting with Goalmaxxing on July 15

  • A ticket to our annual Summit conference in February 2027

Your membership also covers the event costs and overhead that keep Sarasota Tech going, which is why we created the tier in the first place. More than 350 community members have already joined. Between a year of SIGs and a Summit ticket, the math is easy.

Already a premium member? Register for Goalmaxxing now.

Not yet? Join today and Goalmaxxing is included, along with every SIG that follows and the Summit in February.

Three years ago, Sarasota Tech started with a simple observation: this city has plenty of tech talent, it's just spread across isolated teams and remote desks. Everything above is what happens when it gets connected.

As always, thank you for your support and your ideas. They shape what we build next. See you on the 15th.

posts.title: May Community Updates
posts.summary: Here is what the Sarasota Tech community is up to this month.
posts.body:
Hello Sarasota Tech friends 👋🏽.

May Tech JAM

Our next Tech JAM will be on May 21st at Aloft in downtown Sarasota. This venue is always a crowd favorite.  You can look forward to light bites, cold drinks and a live DJ.  We will share a special announcement about one of our founding board members and a few updates about our evolving leadership structure. 

Be sure to register, so that we know you are coming. Registrations are already approaching 200 people, so it should be a great event.  Don’t miss out on some of the best networking in Sarasota!

April Recap:

Last month we moved outdoors to see the latest developments in SportsTech. We held our event at the new Sarasota Paradise facility in Lakewood Ranch. If you aren’t familiar with the Paradise, they are our own professional soccer team here in Sarasota.

Attendees had the opportunity to network and later take a tour of the sports complex. The primary presentation was delivered by Head Coach Mika Elovaara. Mika walked us through how the Sarasota Paradise collects hundreds of data points on each player’s performance during games. They then correlate the player data to actual game outcomes. This allows the coaching staff to work with players to optimize their performance.

For example, if a forward player spends more time in a particular zone around the opposing goal, that usually results in a higher score rate for that player. This seems like a simple observation, but can have a significant outcome on game scores. This methodology is applied across all player types, whether forwards, mid-fielders, defenders and even the goalie. The magnitude of data collection is significant and the Paradise has a unique relationship with a proprietary platform for processing it, called Playmaker.AI.

Thanks again to the Sarasota Paradise leadership team for hosting us! If you are a soccer fan, their games are a lot of fun. You can view the team’s schedule on the club’s website. They host games through the summer and fall.

posts.title: 2026 Giving Challenge: Support the Nonprofits that Support Us
posts.summary: Mark your calendar for the upcoming 2026 Giving Challenge!
posts.body:
Our Sarasota Tech community includes several nonprofit and education organizations whose support is vital to our success. Now we have an opportunity to show them our support during the 2026 Giving Challenge. 

This 24-hour fundraising event is a great way to give back. Your online donation of $25 to $100 will be matched 1:1 between noon April 15 and noon April 16, 2026. 

We’re excited to shine a spotlight on the nonprofits that are participating in this important local fundraising event. Click on the nonprofit name to visit their fundraising page, and set a reminder to donate starting at noon April 15. 

FUNducation: Led by Sarasota.Tech board member Neirda Thompson-Pemberton, FUNducation is on a mission to expose, engage, and inspire our youth to be the innovators of tomorrow through education in Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics (STEAM). They are bringing Boston Dynamics and Spot to two events you can attend on April 15. RSVP 

Mote Marine Laboratory: Mote is working to protect and restore our precious marine resources. Mote science is leading to new discoveries, and Mote is translating that science to promote greater understanding of and appreciation for the marine environment.

New College Foundation (Applied Data Science Program): New College’s Master’s in Applied Data Science program is a rigorous exploration of Databases & Computing, Data Visualization & Statistics and Machine Learning & AI.

Ringling College of Art and Design: For 95 years, Ringling College of Art and Design has been where talent, innovation, and imagination come alive. Every day, our students, faculty, and alumni use their creativity to shape industries, strengthen communities, and enrich lives.

Sarasota Chamber Foundation: The purpose of the Greater Sarasota Chamber of Commerce Foundation is to conduct workforce, educational training, and leadership development programs, all while being a voice for the business community and community as a whole. 

State College of Florida Foundation: Our mission is to connect donors’ passions and regional partners with State College of Florida’s outstanding students, faculty, programs, and community.

Suncoast Science Center/Faulhaber Fab Lab: Fab Lab’s high school student instructors create hands-on STEAM experiences that build confidence, curiosity, and real-world skills through near-peer mentorship.

University of South Florida Foundation (Muma College of Business): The Giving Challenge is hosted by the Community Foundation of Sarasota County, with giving strengthened by The Patterson Foundation.

Shoutout to all the other nonprofit and education organizations in the Sarasota Tech community, including the City of Sarasota, Florida High Tech Corridor, and University of Florida.

posts.title: The Sarasota Tech Summit Agenda Is Live — Here’s What to Expect
posts.summary: The agenda for the Sarasota Tech Summit is officially live, and it’s shaping up to be one of the most energizing tech events in Florida.
posts.body:
This isn’t a conference built around buzzwords or surface-level AI talks. The Sarasota Tech Summit is designed for founders, operators, technologists, marketers, students, and community leaders who want real insight into how technology is being built, applied, and scaled right now—and where it’s headed over the next few years.

What’s on the Agenda

The day is intentionally structured to balance inspiration, education, and connection:

  • Keynotes from builders and operators who are actively scaling companies

  • Panels that go beyond the basics, including honest conversations around AI’s upside, risks, and real-world impact

  • Breakout-style sessions focused on execution, not theory

  • Student and early-career perspectives alongside seasoned founders and executives

  • Plenty of networking time with people actually building in the region

Hands on Workshops

Startup School

Experts in venture capital, software development, branding, business formation, intellectual property rights, accounting, finance + more will be on site running small group breakouts and interactive workshops.

Quick Pitch

Are you looking for financing or feedback on your startup? Sign up for our Quick Pitch to put your concepts to the test in a fast paced competition with real time feedback from a panel of experienced investors.

Demo Stations

Are you working on something interesting and want to show it off? A robotics project, new software, game, 3D print or hardware? Fill out the form below and we might invite you to demo it live at the Summit.

What to participate in the Startup School, Quick Pitch and/or Demo Station? Fill out this form.

Why This Summit Is Different

What makes the Sarasota Tech Summit unique is its community-first approach. It brings together local and national voices while staying rooted in real operator experience. You’ll hear what’s working, what’s broken, and what leaders would do differently if they were starting again today.

Whether you’re running a company, thinking about starting one, leading technology inside an organization, or exploring what a career in tech could look like, this agenda is built to meet you where you are.

Don’t Wait

Tickets are already moving quickly, and once they’re gone, they’re gone. Last year sold out with a waiting list—and this year’s agenda raises the bar even higher.

You can view the full agenda and secure your spot here:
👉 https://sarasota.tech/summit

If you care about where technology, business, and community intersect in Florida, this is a day worth putting on your calendar.

posts.title: Kicking off Season 3 of Sarasota Tech
posts.summary: Sarasota Tech Announces New Board Members, Reveals 2026 Tech Summit Plans, and Expands Community Programming
posts.body:
Sarasota, FL — September 2025 — Sarasota Tech, the grassroots organization fueling the growth of Sarasota’s innovation ecosystem, announced three new board members and unveiled details for its highly anticipated 2026 Tech Summit. The announcements mark the beginning of Sarasota Tech’s third year of monthly meetups and community-driven programming.

Founded in 2023 by a small group of local entrepreneurs, Sarasota Tech has grown from a few friends in a bar to hundreds of tech professionals gathering at different locations around town each month. With no marketing budget or paid advertising, the group has expanded purely through word-of-mouth, hosting 31 events with more than 3,000 attendees over the last two years. The group is making waves as one of Florida’s fastest growing tech communities, drawing attendees from as far as Tampa, Orlando and Miami.

“What started with six of us in a bar has now become a network of thousands,” said Raymmar Tirado, Sarasota Tech co-founder. “As we enter our third year, we’re excited to bring new energy to the board, expand our programming, and double down on putting Sarasota on the map as a place for technological innovation”

Joining the founding board are Neirda Pemberton, Jennifer Jensen, and Peter Offringa, who will help shape Sarasota Tech’s next phase of growth. Together with co-founders Raymmar Tirado, Pete Petersen, Toli Marchuk and Vlad Ljesevic, the board will focus on expanding community events, preparing for the annual Tech Summit, and using technology to connect the community.

Sarasota Tech Summit 2026

The second annual Sarasota Tech Summit will take January 15, 2026, at the brand-new Mote SEA (Science Education Aquarium). The event will feature a world-class expo hall, interactive labs, breakout sessions, panel discussions and a rooftop VIP party. Organizers expect more than 500 attendees, up from 350 at the inaugural summit earlier this year.

Programming will include:

  • Daytime Workshops & Labs — Pitch deck coaching, investor meetups and founder networking along with other hands-on sessions.

  • Evening Keynotes & Panels — Spotlighting the regions most innovative founders, technologists, and investors.

  • Networking & Afterparty — Rooftop reception & VIP afterparty

“This summit isn’t just about Sarasota,” said Pete Petersen, Sarasota Tech co-founder. “We want to position this city as a marquee destination for tech professionals in Florida. The goal is to grow into a multi-day conference that brings thousands of people here—founders, builders, and innovators from across the state.”

Membership and Sponsorship Opportunities

Sarasota Tech recently launched a new member directory and online platform to help connect attendees. Members can create profiles and upgrade to an annual membership ($200), which includes a corporate listing in the new directory as well as a ticket to the annual summit (regularly $250).

Sponsorship opportunities are now open for the 2026 Tech Summit. Last year’s event sold out, and this year’s expanded venue offers sponsors even greater visibility in front of a fast-growing network of entrepreneurs, technologists, and investors.

About Sarasota Tech

Sarasota Tech is a community-led nonprofit dedicated to building Sarasota into a premier hub for technology and innovation. Through monthly meetups, annual summits, and ongoing programming, Sarasota Tech connects founders, developers, investors, and operators to accelerate the region’s entrepreneurial ecosystem.

For sponsorships, speaking opportunities, or membership inquiries, reach out to info@sarasota.tech or visit Sarasota.tech

posts.title: Season 3 Preview - Sarasota Tech
posts.summary: Get a sneak peek at what we are working on and what comes next with Sarasota Tech.
posts.body:
This August marks two years since we hosted our first official Sarasota Tech event and it has been one hell of a ride. If I am being honest, I don’t think any of us who were there in the early days expected this group to evolve into what it is today.

What started as a small meetup in a local bar has become a thriving community and captured the attention of our entire region.

Over the last two years we have:

  • Hosted 22 events drawing close to 3,000 attendees!

  • Sold out our first Tech Summit with 300+ attendees

  • Formed a 501c6 and became an official nonprofit

  • Raised more than $70,000 from founding members, ticket sales & sponsors

And the crazy part? We did this all with $0 spent on marketing or advertisings along the way.

The growth of this organization has been 100% word-of-mouth which means you are as much a part of this success as we are.

These early numbers make it clear that there is a significant demand for this type of community in our region and we plan to keep pushing the limits of what this organization can become.

But before we move forward full steam ahead we want to take a step back and make sure we lay a proper foundation for Season 3 of Sarasota Tech.

A new chapter focused on scaling impact, deepening relationships, and creating stronger systems to support our momentum.

Here’s a snapshot of what’s ahead:

1. Expanding the Board

We’ve officially expanded our board with three new members who we will announce before our next event. Each brings a unique perspective and network that aligns with our trajectory and we’re excited to invite them into our strategic planning.

2. Evolving the Format

We’re using the summer to pause large public events and focus on internal strategy. Instead of our typical July or August meetup, we’re planning a Season 3 launch in September. Expect a revamped cadence of events, improved planning, and more intentional programming with a focus on small groups and more intimate connections.

3. Empowering the Community

We’re building out our infrastructure to support more community-led initiatives including small group meetups, interest-driven events, and invite-only gatherings. Our aim is to create a platform that other community leaders can plug into, while we focus on coordination, amplification, and content distribution.

4. Sarasota Tech Summit: January 2026

Planning has already begun for our next flagship event. Targeting 500+ attendees, we're exploring exciting new venues and sponsorship opportunities. If you’re interested in sponsoring or collaborating, now’s the time to get involved.

5. Platform & Comms

We’re thinking about how to improve internal systems to better support member communication, onboarding, and access control. This includes:

  • A new public newsletter and board updates via our website

  • Better tooling for small group leaders to connect with members

  • More organized documentation and processes for community contributors

Thank you for your patience as we take some time to properly set ourselves up for long term success.

We will likely share a survey soon asking for more specific feedback but for now you can share any thoughts you might have about the group by replying to this message or sending an email to info@sarasota.tech.

If you're part of the community and want to get more involved, now’s a great time to raise your hand. We’re only as strong as the people who show up to help us build and there is much left to build.

Raymmar Tirado
Chairman, Sarasota Tech

posts.title: A Resounding Success: Highlights from Our Recent Tech Summit
posts.summary: With more than 300 attendees, our first sold-out tech summit surpassed all expectations.
posts.body:
Jan 9, 2025 we hosted our highly anticipated Tech Summit, and the results surpassed all expectations. The standing room only event left no doubt about the appetite for innovation and connection in our local tech community.

Here are a few write-ups from the community about the event:

  • Writeup from the Tampa Bay Business Journal

  • Writeup on linkedIn

Rave Reviews from Attendees

The event was electric from start to finish with back to back sessions ranging from is Sarasota Investable, to Emerging Tech Trends along with insights on what it takes to move the city forward.

Great event! I’ve been to events in another city and it was never about building up the community/tech scene. People here seem to genuinely want to help each other where in other places it was more about “what can you do for me?”

"Your team was incredible, loved the insights from all the panelists. Excited for what’s happening now."

"Great event! Congratulations to all of you for putting this together and thanks for your hard work."

"Great turn out. Great energy. Kudos to... the founders for an amazing event. Surpassed expectations."

The success of this summit wouldn’t have been possible without the incredible support from our Sponsors and general community.

From the attendees who brought their energy and curiosity, to the speakers who generously shared their expertise, to our dedicated team who worked tirelessly behind the scenes—this was truly a collective effort.

Looking Ahead

While we’re still riding high from the success of this summit, we’re already thinking about how to make the next one even better. Your passion fuels our mission to create impactful events, and we can’t wait to continue this journey with you.

Thank you to everyone who joined us and made this event unforgettable. Stay tuned for more exciting announcements—the best is yet to come!

posts.title: Sarasota Tech Summit 2025
posts.summary: Can Sarasota Become a “Tech Town"?
posts.body:
Sarasota, FL — Sarasota Tech is excited to announce the inaugural Sarasota Tech Summit in collaboration with the Economic Development Corporation of Sarasota County and the Truist Foundation. 

The event is set to take place on January 9, 2025, from 5:00 PM to 10:00 PM at the Art Ovation Hotel in downtown Sarasota. This premier event aims to bring together over 200 tech professionals, investors, and thought leaders from across the region, to explore pivotal topics shaping the future of technology.

Attendees will engage in discussions on subjects such as the investability of Sarasota startups, the multifaceted impacts of artificial intelligence, and the potential for Sarasota to emerge as a leading tech hub. The summit will also feature a Tech Town Hall, providing an open forum for community dialogue.

General admission includes a taco bar, cash bar, display area, networking opportunities with top regional tech professionals and investors, along with insights into current tech trends. VIP ticket holders will enjoy all general admission benefits, a VIP meet-and-greet before the event as well as entry to a rooftop afterparty with a complimentary drink ticket.

Early bird discounts are available through December 20, offering 25% off any ticket purchase with the code EARLY25. 

Tickets can be purchased at https://lu.ma/r21g3q5c?coupon=EARLY25 

The Sarasota Tech Summit is made possible by the generous support of sponsors such as the Economic Development Corporation of Sarasota County and the Truist Foundation, along with numerous startup and advisory sponsors.
